question: Down 14, a team scores a touchdown. Should it go for two right away or kick?
answer: Go for 2. Given two TDs and a stop it wins 59% of the time against 46% for kicking, worth +3.2 points of win chance overall.
findings: The gain given two TDs is +13.3 points (+10.8 to +15.7), and going for 2 first wins as long as the 2-pt rate is above 35.2%.
After a Q4 PAT at down 8 the same team scored the next TD with nothing between in 24% (n=199); in the rest the choice decides almost nothing.
Inputs: 2-pt 48.1% (n=1,476), XP 94.4% (n=14,843), and teams that tied late won 47% in overtime (n=161).
Teams went for 2 at down 8 in the 4th in 0 of 35 in 2015-16 and 16 of 30 in 2025-26.
Raw results are noisy: teams that went for 2 won 5 of 48 and teams that kicked won 19 of 151, and the teams that chose each differ.
method: A closed-form tree given two TDs and no opponent score: after 2 is good, kick to win; after 2 fails, 2 again to tie; after an XP, kick to tie; overtime at 50%. The CI comes from Beta draws of the 2-pt and XP rates. The game-level edge is the share of down-8 spots that reach a second TD first, times the gain.
data: nflverse play-by-play, 2015 to 2026; 1,476 2-pt tries, 14,843 XPs, 199 Q4 PATs at down 8.
split_check: The gain is +13.1 points with the 2015-20 rates (2-pt 47.6%) and +13.5 with the 2021-26 rates (2-pt 48.6%); with the measured overtime rate it is +15.1.
